text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly over many months or years, and many people have mild or no symptoms in the early stages. When early signs do appear, they are usually subtle and easy to miss.
snippet_highlighted_words: they are usually subtle and easy to miss

list.snippet: Increased Thirst (Polydipsia): You feel unusually thirsty even after drinking water, because high blood sugar pulls fluid out of your tissues.
Frequent Urination (Polyuria): You need to pee more often, especially at night, as your kidneys work overtime to filter and flush out the extra glucose.
Persistent Fatigue: You feel constantly tired or drained because your body's cells cannot properly absorb and use glucose for energy.
Increased Hunger: You feel hungry shortly after eating because your cells are starved for the energy they cannot process.
Blurred Vision: High blood sugar causes fluid to shift into the lenses of your eyes, making it hard to focus.
Slow-Healing Sores or Cuts: Cuts, scrapes, or minor bruises take a long time to heal due to poor circulation and a weakened immune response.
Frequent Infections: You experience recurring skin infections, gum disease, or urinary tract infections (UTIs) because excess sugar feeds bacteria and yeast.
Numbness or Tingling: You feel a prickling, numbness, or burning sensation in your hands or feet (peripheral neuropathy).
Darkened Skin Patches: You notice dark, velvety patches of skin (called acanthosis nigricans), most commonly around your neck, armpits, or groin, which is a sign of insulin resistance.
Unexplained Weight Changes: You might experience unexpected weight loss (as the body burns muscle and fat for fuel) or subtle weight gain around the abdomen.

text_blocks.snippet: Because symptoms can be so quiet, doctors rely on simple blood tests to confirm if you have type 2 diabetes or prediabetes:

list.snippet: Fasting Plasma Glucose Test: Measures blood sugar after an 8-hour fast; a result of 126 mg/dL or higher indicates diabetes.
A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar level over the past 2 to 3 months; a result of 6.5% or higher indicates diabetes.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures blood sugar at any time without fasting; a result of 200 mg/dL or higher points to diabetes.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about symptoms and diagnostic standards through the Mayo Clinic Type 2 Diabetes Guide or the Cleveland Clinic Type 2 Diabetes Overview.
